what_it_does: Basilisk is a complete, working computer chip designed entirely with free, open-source software tools—something rarely achieved at production scale. The team built a 64-bit RISC-V processor (the open-source instruction set architecture) that can run full Linux on a single chip in 2024 technology, together with memory interfaces, USB connectivity, and video output. The chip is about the size of a postage stamp (34 square millimeters) and demonstrates that open-source chip design can compete with commercial tools by showing 2-3x faster design time and smaller final area through careful tuning of the design process.
